data.narrative:
Electric Era, led by founder Quincy Lee, is a Series A climate and energy company seeking valuation following $11.5M in total raised capital. The valuation universe comprises nine same-sector peers: one public company (LNZA) and eight private firms including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen.

Stage-progression analysis forms the primary applicable method. Using total raised ($11.5M) as a valuation proxy, a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A progression yields an implied valuation of $23M. Peer-median triangulation was not applicable due to insufficient narrow-stage comparables within Climate & Energy; while nine sector peers exist, none yielded three or more datapoints within same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier filters. A broader sector median would introduce unacceptable dispersion.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $20M (low) to $26M (high), with $23M as the median. This range rests on a single methodology, which constrains confidence. Key uncertainties include the appropriateness of the 2.0x multiplier for Electric Era's specific market conditions and capital efficiency, the lack of directly comparable Series A-stage peers to validate stage progression, and execution risk not captured in raised capital alone. Additional diligence on unit economics, competitive positioning within Climate & Energy, and founder track record would strengthen conviction in this range.
